blockingIssues.problem: Claim of visitor satisfaction (idea title and rationale) vs. source limitation. The idea's title and rationale state that printed routes “keep museum visitors satisfied” or “protect the visitor experience,” but the source explicitly reports that staff “did not track visitor satisfaction.”
blockingIssues.correction: Remove or soften any asserted satisfaction or protection claims. Rephrase to a supported, observational statement such as: “Printed indoor routes provide a substitute indoor option when the sculpture garden is closed,” and in the rationale note that 38 handouts were issued but no satisfaction or completion data were collected.

blockingIssues.problem: Overgeneralization from tested instance to a broader class (title scope) vs. source scope. The idea's title makes a broad claim about “weather closures,” while the source frames the situation specifically as closures “for high water” (flooding) and reports on two wet Sunday openings.
blockingIssues.correction: Limit the scope to the documented setting. Change the title and any general wording to specify the tested case, e.g. “Printed indoor routes provide a fallback when the sculpture garden is closed for high water,” or otherwise explicitly state that evidence comes from two wet openings in April.

blockingIssues.problem: Missing precondition for visitors vs. source instruction. The idea is addressed to visitors planning to see the garden but omits the source's explicit instruction that “Visitors should still check the same-day garden notice before travelling.”
blockingIssues.correction: Include the source's precondition in the audience guidance: advise readers to check the same-day garden notice before travelling and present the printed route as a fallback for days when the garden is closed for high water.
